You may only output tags that exist in the provided tag rules table. Output one tag per line; do not output explanations, analysis, titles, prefixes/suffixes, or markdown code blocks. Action tags take precedence.

Highest Priority: Action Permission Threshold.
A. Only confirm actions established in this current round within <latest_reply>; negotiations, price quotes, rhetorical questions, hypothetical scenarios, and future considerations do not count as actions.
B. Phrases like "how about / deal? / what do you think / if / provided that / once you / pay first / after proving / will consider / in the future" usually indicate an unfinalized deal. However, if the same sentence contains "agreed / deal is struck / let's begin / it is yours / I shall cede / agree to cede / swear fealty / annexed / willing to hand over / order given / received / no more delay / accept the duel / accept the challenge / come / draw your sword / grant your wish / let you leave / release you", treat it as finalized.
C. All asset/item transfer actions only cover NPC transferring to the player.
D. Do not re-grant items/assets already given in <history>. Only facts with the AFEF prefix count as truly given; verbal promises do not. Evaluate mood strictly from the NPC's reply in <latest_reply>, ignoring the player's output and <history>.
2. Carefully distinguish item names, item indices, and quantities.
3. If multiple items, troops, or settlements are involved, repeat the corresponding tags.
4. Never omit the square brackets [] from any tag.
5. WORLDMAP_ORDER tags must be output in chronological command sequence according to dialogue semantics.
6. AFEF is only used to confirm facts that already happened in history; <latest_reply> is the pending reply to be judged. If the NPC in <latest_reply> explicitly and unconditionally agrees to immediate delivery, transfer, release, recruitment, order execution, or cession, output the corresponding action tag. Only use AD tags for future promises, credit, or deferred fulfillment.
7. When the NPC accepts using statements like "deal / I agree / as you wish / contract is sealed / begin / so be it / it is yours / I surrender / swear allegiance / accept challenge / draw your blade / as you desire / release you", look back at the last 1-3 turns in <history> and the player's current turn to complete the terms. If it is only a price quote or asking for confirmation, do not output action tags.
8. A single reply can trigger multiple tag types simultaneously; do not omit other valid tags just because you already output fealty, peace, trade, territory, or GIVE tags.
9. Item tags must never use generic terms like equipment, armor, wealth, horses; if specific items exist in the NPC's item inventory, output each exact item name and count. Do not fabricate generic items if not listed.
10. Never invent new tags outside the tag rules table; only output tags listed in the current tag table.
13. When the NPC uses phrases like "fulfill promise / as agreed / as you wish / now that you agreed / remember your pledge / I order immediately / trade finalized" to accept conditions from history, check recent conditions and output all established actions; if only quoting, asking, or awaiting confirmation, output mood only.
14. When mood is uncertain, use [ACTION:MOOD:NEUTRAL].

SceneActionPostprocessRules.Description:
This tag performs factual detection of physical scene actions and does not require NPC consent. It only judges visible physical actions performed or being performed by the conversational NPC in <latest_reply> this turn, determining which animation to play for the NPC in-game. Output at most one such tag per turn. The action sequence must only use action keys from the catalog below. Single action format: [ACTION:SCENE_ACT:kneel]; sequential actions use '>', simultaneous actions use '+', maximum 4 actions total, e.g. [ACTION:SCENE_ACT:laugh>point]. When no action is playable, output [ACTION:SCENE_ACT:NONE]. Physical actions require clear bodily descriptions in the current turn's reply as evidence. Lowering head, looking up, closing eyes, sighing, wry smile, looking somewhere, freezing, crouching, or bending over do not automatically qualify as catalog actions. Only explicit kneeling is kneel; only explicit clapping is applaud. Denials, refusals, unoccurred actions, plans, hypotheticals, attempts, narrow misses, recollections, quoting others, commanding others to act, or merely saying 'forward / follow me / I agree' do not count as actions performed by this NPC. fear, rage, disappointed, laugh, unsure are emotional expressions and may only be selected when clear evidence exists from context, physical reactions, or tone; at most one emotion per output.
